title: The /pr Skill: PR bodies with a visual summary, before/after evidence, and a one-way/two-way door call
summary: Matt Pocock explains his `pr` skill, which defines the shape of a pull request body: Summary (smallest useful visual), Evidence (before and after), and Merge Danger (one-way vs two-way door plus blast radius). It also covers limits: the agent grading its own door call is suspect, and the skill only writes the body.

principles.text: A PR summary should be a visual of the change's shape, not a prose description of the diff.
principles.quote: The summary is a visual, not a paragraph.

principles.text: Pick the smallest view that makes the key point clear and keep surrounding words brief.
principles.quote: This one picks the **smallest view** that makes the key point clear (pseudocode, a call tree, a component tree, a file tree, a Mermaid diagram, or a shaped diff) and keeps the words around it brief.

principles.text: Evidence must be a before and after (screenshot, failing-then-passing test, changed output), not a claim that tests pass.
principles.quote: "Tests are green" on its own is a claim, not a before and after.

principles.text: State whether a change is a one-way or two-way door so reviewers can disagree with an explicit claim and spend attention accordingly.
principles.quote: It changes "is this safe to merge?" from a gut feeling into a stated claim the reviewer can disagree with.

principles.text: Be most suspicious of the agent's own 'two-way, small blast radius' call, since the author is grading its own change.
principles.quote: The agent that wrote the change is the one grading it, so be most suspicious when it says "two-way, small blast radius".

principles.text: Give the agent the ticket or spec, not just the diff, and document your repo's always-one-way changes where it will read them.
principles.quote: make sure the agent has the [ticket](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/ticket) or [spec](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/spec) in front of it, not just the diff
